AI Has Changed Digital Citizenship Forever

Your students are already online. They are already at risk.

Let’s equip them with the skills to navigate the digital world safely and wisely.

Students now need more than basic digital skills. They must learn to question AI-generated content, recognize misinformation, protect their privacy, think critically, and use AI responsibly.

CBSE Requirements

CBSE Circulars Skill-81/2025 and Acad-39/2026 reinforce the importance of digital citizenship and cyber safety. Schools now need a structured way to deliver these skills and demonstrate meaningful implementation.

Students are at risk now

Students encounter cyberbullying, scams, deepfakes, AI-generated content and misinformation. Schools have an important role in preparing students to recognize these risks and respond responsibly.

Teachers need the right support

Digital safety requires current content, age-appropriate learning, assessments and practical resources. A ready-to-use framework enables teachers to deliver this effectively without adding another curriculum-design burden.

Readiness needs to be measurable

Schools already assess readiness across areas such as fire safety, health and physical well-being. Digital readiness deserves the same structured approach, with a clear benchmark for students’ ability to navigate the digital world safely and responsibly.

COMPUDON Junior is the structured, ready-to-deploy program that closes this gap.

Neuropsychologist-reviewed curriculum, assessments, student reports, school benchmarks, certificates, and national recognition. Less than 10 hours of total coordinator effort. ₹699 per student, all inclusive. No hidden fees.

Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions, answered

Who can participate?

Children aged 8-14 (Grades 3-9), split into Explorers (Grades 3-5) and Navigators (Grades 6-9) categories, each with age-appropriate learning resources and assessments.

How much does it cost?

Season VII participation is ₹699 per student through a participating school (₹1,499 for direct individual registration), paid only once. This covers curriculum and learning resources, practice exams, the Level 1 examination, the Level 2/India Final examination if qualified, and prizes and recognition. There are no hidden upgrade fees; optional preparation material may be offered ahead of the Level 2 round but is not required.

How much coordinator effort is required?

Minimal. In our experience, less than 10 hours across the championship. We handle parent and student communication, provide access to the Learning Management System, assessment logistics, report generation, and all other activities. The coordinating teacher's role, as we see it, is limited to ensuring parents and students know about this and register, scheduling the assessment window, and ensuring students write the exam within the appointed time.

Can parents register directly?

Yes, whether or not the school is participating. Students from participating schools get the lower ₹699 fee; direct individual registration is ₹1,499 - see the Students page for details.

What does the school receive?

Schools receive complete study materials, an assessment platform, student guides, a school dashboard with real-time progress visibility, benchmarked readiness reports, and a School Future Readiness Report that leadership can present to boards and parents.

Prashast Prajapati — Sanskaar Valley School, Bhopal

I still remember my first attempt at COMPUDON Junior championship. I'd made the merit list, but there was no trophy or medal. At the time, it felt like the end of the world.

But I came back the next year. And the year after that.

Over time, COMPUDON Junior stopped being just another competition for me. It became the place where I discovered I was good at technology. Every challenge taught me something new, pushed me to think differently, and gave me more confidence. Long before I was building projects or writing real code, it made me believe in myself.

Today, I'm in Grade 11, preparing for JEE with the goal of studying Computer Science at IIT. Since those early competitions, I've earned 10 Microsoft certifications, built several technology projects, and won multiple national-level technology competitions. Looking back, I can honestly say that my journey began with COMPUDON.

If I had let that first disappointment stop me, I would have missed everything that came after.

So, if you're thinking about participating, take the chance. You might win a trophy. You might not.

Either way, you'll learn a lot of new things, you will challenge yourself, meet other students who share your passion for technology, and discover you're capable of much more than you think.

One attempt may not change your life, but it could be the first step toward something much bigger.

It certainly was for me.
